scope: Native clients (no emulator) through the native C bridge, unchanged companions and an unchanged world server with the ownership store: each legacy save enrolled through the running game (revision 1), client A walks and saves (revision 2, the canonical save holds the position A's game reported), both games closed (each game's own save file holds its canonical player state), both started again (Continue restores each saved map and position, new host leases and game incarnations, the players see each other) and both save again against their last revision (A 3, B 2); host store integrity check; source saves unchanged. Every save byte moves through the ROM's save mailbox and 4 KiB save window. Ordinary key presses on each client's own X display. Runs marked recover=true also apply A's canonical save to its running game after unsaved walking (live recovery: the save mailbox's write path, 1024 staged 128-byte chunks, commit and read-back); A's game must be back at the saved position without a restart or a new lease.
note: The companion verifies the GBA ROM and manifest of the same engine source; the native executable is a separate artefact of that source, identified by game_sha256.
